title: Kestrel Med Sync Group Rules: One Shared Sync Day per Patient
content:
Under Auto Refill & Medication Sync, all of a patient's open Med Sync enrollments form one sync group sharing one sync day. The Med Sync programs are Kestrel Med Sync Monthly, Kestrel Med Sync 90-Day and Kestrel Med Sync with Adherence Packaging; an enrollment is open while it is in enrolled, active or paused status.

## Rules of the sync group

1. **One day for the group.** The group shares one sync day, a day of the month no earlier than the program's earliest allowed sync day and no later than its latest allowed sync day, both ends included.
2. **Who chooses it.** The sync day is chosen under the program's sync-day rule: by the patient where the program leaves the choice to the patient, by the pharmacist where it leaves the choice to the pharmacist.
3. **Changing it.** Changing the sync day for one enrollment changes it for the whole group. The sync day is changed at most the program's allowed number of times per program year.
4. **Auto Refill gives way to the group.** A patient who joins any Med Sync program has every open Auto Refill enrollment — in Kestrel Auto Refill 30-Day, Kestrel Auto Refill 90-Day or Kestrel Home Delivery Auto Refill — for a med-sync-eligible prescription ended as program change and re-enrolled in the sync group, so that Auto Refill and Med Sync never run on the same patient's eligible prescriptions at the same time. A med-sync-eligible prescription is one whose handling class has the Med Sync eligible switch of the Prescriptions charter set to true.
5. **Joining mid-cycle.** A prescription joining the group mid-cycle follows the program's mid-cycle handling for a new prescription: a short fill to the sync day, or addition at the next cycle, as the program provides.

## Condition and result

| Condition | Result |
|---|---|
| The patient holds more than one open Med Sync enrollment | All of them share one sync day |
| The sync day is changed on one enrollment of the group | Every enrollment of the group takes the new day; the change counts against the program's yearly allowance of changes |
| The patient joins any Med Sync program while holding an open Auto Refill enrollment for a med-sync-eligible prescription | That Auto Refill enrollment ends as program change and the prescription is re-enrolled in the sync group |
| A prescription joins the group mid-cycle | It follows the program's mid-cycle handling |

## Illustration (hypothetical patient)

A hypothetical patient holds an open Kestrel Auto Refill 30-Day enrollment for a prescription whose class is Med Sync eligible and an open Kestrel Auto Refill 90-Day enrollment for a prescription whose class is not Med Sync eligible. The patient then joins Kestrel Med Sync Monthly with two other prescriptions, with a sync day on the 12th.

- The two Kestrel Med Sync Monthly enrollments form the patient's sync group and share the 12th.
- The Kestrel Auto Refill 30-Day enrollment is an open Auto Refill enrollment for a med-sync-eligible prescription, so it is ended as program change and that prescription is re-enrolled in the sync group, sharing the 12th.
- The Kestrel Auto Refill 90-Day enrollment is for a prescription that is not med-sync-eligible, so rule 4 does not reach it.
- If the sync day of one enrollment of the group is later moved to the 20th, every enrollment of the group moves to the 20th. The 20th lies within the allowed range of each Med Sync program; the 30th would not.
